title: Circuit Judge, 9th Judicial Circuit, Group 1
what_it_does: Circuit judges hear felony criminal cases, major civil suits, family and probate matters. This seat is elected by voters across the 9th Circuit (Orange, Osceola). Nonpartisan; a candidate needs a majority, and this contest was not decided in August.
verified_ballot_note: Candidate list taken from the Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list on 2026-09-18 (https://dos.elections.myflorida.com/candidates/CanList.asp); both candidates are marked Qualified, which for a nonpartisan seat means the August vote did not produce a majority winner (or the seat is decided only in November). Positions have not been researched; check the county Supervisor of Elections sample ballot.

candidates.name: Temika Hampton-Johnson
candidates.photo_source: Ballotpedia candidate photo (downloaded copy in assets/photos)
candidates.occupation: Attorney in private practice; former assistant public defender and former probation and parole officer
candidates.background: Hampton-Johnson is an Orlando-area attorney in private practice who previously worked as a public defender and, before that, as a probation and parole officer. She holds a J.D. from the Florida A&M University College of Law and an MBA and a BBA in accounting from Stetson University. She co-chairs the City of Orlando Civil Service Board, serves on the board of The LGBT+ Center Orlando, and has volunteered with Legal Aid since 2013 and with the Florida Rights Restoration effort. She led the August 18, 2026 primary for 9th Circuit Group 1 with 46.3%, ahead of incumbent Judge Mikaela Nix, and advanced to a November 3 runoff against Charles Hart.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

other_issues.title: Judicial approach
other_issues.summary: In her 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey Hampton-Johnson says she would decide matters on the facts, evidence and binding precedent, free from political influence or personal bias, and would treat every person the same regardless of race, sex, sexual orientation or economic status.

other_issues.title: Policy positions declined
other_issues.summary: Hampton-Johnson says judicial canons prohibit her from taking positions on political policy issues, and that within the court system she is focused on improving access to the courts and restoring public trust in the judiciary.

record.item: J.D., Florida A&M University College of Law; MBA and BBA in accounting, Stetson University. Career as a probation and parole officer, then assistant public defender, then private practice; hundreds of pro bono hours as a Legal Aid volunteer since 2013.

sources.title: Orange County 9th Circuit Judge Group 1 - 2026, VOTE411 Voter Guide

record.item: Co-chair of the City of Orlando Civil Service Board and board member of The LGBT+ Center Orlando. No judicial experience.

record.item: Received 76,618 votes (46.30%) in the August 18, 2026 primary, forcing a November runoff.

candidates.name: Charles Hart
candidates.occupation: Attorney, Charles C. Hart Law Office, Sanford (criminal and guardianship law); Florida Supreme Court certified family law and county court mediator
candidates.background: Hart practices criminal and guardianship law from an office in Sanford and opened a mediation practice after being certified by the Florida Supreme Court as a family law and county court mediator. He previously served as an assistant state attorney and as a public defender in the 18th Judicial Circuit, and taught accounting at the University of South Florida and Santa Fe Community College. He holds a B.S. in accounting and an M.A. in accounting from the University of South Florida, a B.A. in political science from the University of Florida and a J.D. from the University of Florida's Levin College of Law (2007). He chaired the Orange County Republican Executive Committee from 2018 to 2022 and ran unsuccessfully for the Florida House in 2022. He finished second in the August 18, 2026 primary with 25.7% and declined to complete the News 6 candidate questionnaire.

roster_sources.title: Florida Division of Elections, 2026 general election candidate list

other_issues.title: Judicial approach
other_issues.summary: In his 2026 Ballotpedia Candidate Connection survey Hart says judges should follow the law rather than personal agendas or outside pressure, and that he would approach each case with an open mind and apply the law consistently.

other_issues.title: Policy positions declined
other_issues.summary: Asked what areas of public policy he is passionate about, Hart said a judge's responsibility is not to advance a personal policy agenda but to follow the law and decide each case impartially.

record.item: Applied five times to the Ninth Circuit Judicial Nominating Commission and once to the Seventh Circuit, never advancing past the commission; has no prior judicial experience.

Chaired the Orange County Republican Executive Committee from 2018 to 2022 and was a 2022 Republican primary candidate for Florida House District 39; a member of the Federalist Society and a lifetime NRA member. He was a party to a lawsuit over Orange County's COVID-19 mask mandate.

positions_note: Judicial candidates in Florida are bound by the Code of Judicial Conduct, which bars them from making statements that commit them on issues likely to come before the court. This guide therefore does not code positions for them and does not score them in the matching tool. Compare them on experience, background and the record below instead.
